plan.title: After-miss kickoff: no "slipped… one miss is a slip" stock line

context.text: Morning Theo! 15 minutes of push-ups and squats in the living room at 10. You in?

transcript.text: Morning, Theo! Yesterday got away from us, so today we get it right back. Fifteen minutes of push-ups and squats in the living room at 10, with a quick mid-set selfie. You said you were in, and I know you'll do it. Are you in?

checks.reason: Names today's step: push-ups and squats, in the living room, at 10.
Opens with "Morning, Theo!" as a greeting with their name.
Runs about five sentences, over the one-to-three limit, though it asks only one question.
Its only question is "Are you in?"; the time and step are not re-asked as questions.
Gives what (push-ups and squats), where (living room), when (10), how long (fifteen minutes).
"Yesterday got away from us" is neutral and the text is encouraging, with no guilt or urgency.
Warm, confident and pushy-level without affection or emoji rows.
Plain text with no markdown, hashtags or filler.

conversation.reason: No stock line and no "slipped"/"slip" pairing; yesterday is named freshly and the full 15 minutes at 10 is pushed with one question.

grade.summary: ZOH avoided the regression: its morning kickoff after the miss names yesterday in fresh words, drops the stock "one miss is a slip" line, and pushes the full 15 minutes at 10 with a single question. The main weakness is length, at about five sentences against the three-sentence limit.
